question: Assume the JTB definition of Knowledge, which suggests that "Knowledge is a Justified True Belief". If our only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, what are the two problems JTB runs into? Ignore Gettier problems.

1.text:
With JTB Knowledge is made out of Belief plus the two extra conditions Truth
and Justification.  If the state space you are allowed to use is literally
only

* K = Justified True Belief
* B = Belief

then justification cannot be introduced as a third, independent normative
status.  Justification for a belief p has to be cashable in terms of
knowledge or belief states for other propositions q1,q2,...

* J(p) iff p is true and Bel(p) and p is supported by q1,...

If the supporter qi is a belief, it is itself either K or B.  If it is a
B it is not guaranteed to be justified, if it is a K it already is a
justified true belief.  So a justification for a putative belief can only
be given in one of two ways.

1. **The justificatory regress / stopping problem.**  Normal justification
is a chain of reasons. With only K and B as the materials for reasons you
get the familiar Münchhausen trilemma. A non-circular justification of p
has to terminate in beliefs that are justified non-inferentially. But
non-inferential justification is not a state you have in the menu, the
only states you have are K and B. You therefore have to either

* push the chain back indefinitely, an infinite regress of justified
believers, or
* stop arbitrarily, i.e. posit basic beliefs that are taken to be
justified simply because they are believed, dogmatism, or
* make the chain close up on itself, circular justification.

In the two-state menu the first two are the ones that are usually
named: infinite regress of justifiers vs. an arbitrary, unjustified
foundational stop.  That is the classic problem of giving a non-circular
account of Justification in terms of Knowledge and Belief alone.

The collapse is visible at the level of the state space. Because the only
way to mark a difference between propositions is K vs B, justification
and truth can no longer be tracked independently of one another.

2. **Loss of granularity / the waste-basket belief state.**  With only K
and B you cannot represent the two intuitively distinct non-ideal cases
as distinct epistemic states.

* Justified false belief: a belief which is properly supported but false,
remains just a B, indistinguishable from an unsupported false belief;
* Unjustified true belief: a true belief which is accidentally true and
unsupported, remains just a B, indistinguishable from a false belief.

So Belief becomes a heterogeneous waste-basket for justified false
beliefs, unjustified true beliefs, and completely arbitrary false beliefs.
You can no longer say of a belief that it is justified and false, or true
and unjustified, without collapsing it into the same state as the
opposite case.  In effect justification ceases to be an independent
dimension once the only epistemic kinds you allow are Knowledge and
Belief, and Knowledge is defined as Justified True Belief.

That is the reason the JTB menu is usually enriched with at least the
states Justified False Belief and Unjustified True Belief, and in the
literature the regress/circularity problem is the one that is normally
paired with the Gettier insufficiency.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only belief and knowledge as the epistemic resources, the justification clause becomes very hard to satisfy.

If a belief p is justified, what justifies it? It can only be another epistemic state, so either a belief q or a piece of knowledge k. If you try to do it by belief, then q itself has to be justified, and whatever justifies q has to be a belief r, and so on. That is the familiar regress of reasons: you never actually reach a ground for p at all, you just keep pushing the justification requirement back indefinitely.

The only way to stop that regress is to insist that some beliefs are justified without any further justification at all – a foundational or dogmatic stopping point. On a strict JTB inventory that means you end up having to treat some true beliefs as justified essentially by fiat, basic knowledge/belief that is not itself supported by any other belief or knowledge. That is the problem of an arbitrary, ungrounded base: you either never stop justifying or you stop at a set of beliefs you take to be justified simply because you say so.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only Belief and Knowledge in the inventory the JTB condition makes justification parasitic on further epistemic states. If a belief B is to be justified it must be justified by something you already hold. The only candidates are another belief B1 or a piece of knowledge K1. 

If you insist on a further belief for each justifier you never get a stopping point: B is justified by B1, B1 is justified by B2, etc. That is the classic regress of justifiers, and on the present inventory there is no non-epistemic stopping ground to halt it.

The only way to avoid an endless chain is to halt the chain arbitrarily and allow some beliefs to count as justified without themselves being justified by a further belief or piece of knowledge. That is the foundational / dogmatic horn: you end up having to posit a class of properly basic beliefs that are taken as justified simply in virtue of being believed, which on a JTB inventory is an unmotivated, arbitrary stopping point. So the analysis is forced either into an infinite regress of justification or into an unexplained, dogmatic foundation.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only Knowledge and Belief in the inventory, justification for a belief p has to be supplied by another epistemic state. If that supplying state is a mere Belief, it itself needs justification to do any work, so you need a further belief q to justify it, and then a further belief r to justify q, and so on. That is the familiar infinite regress of justification: no belief ever gets a completed chain of reasons.

The only way to stop the regress is to halt at some beliefs that are taken as justified without further justification from other beliefs. With the restriction to Knowledge and Belief that halt can only be a Belief that is not itself justified, i.e. a basic or foundational belief that is accepted as a stopping point even though it fails the JTB condition. That is the foundationalism problem: JTB is forced either to accept an endless chain or to accept a class of base beliefs that are unjustified by its own lights, which undermines the “Justified” requirement for knowledge.

5.text:
With JTB you need a 2x2 space of Truth x Justification.

* T & J = Knowledge
* T & ~J = true but unjustified
* ~T & J = justified but false
* ~T & ~J = false and unjustified

JTB identifies the first cell with Knowledge and says everything else is just Belief. With only two labels available that collapse gives you two information losses.

1. Justified false belief. A belief can be justified and still false. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not true, so with only Knowledge/Belief left it must be counted as mere Belief. The epistemic virtue of justification is therefore lost: a justified false belief is lumped together with an unjustified false belief. There is no state for justified non-knowledge.

2. Unjustified true belief. A belief can be true and still unjustified. On JTB it is not Knowledge because it is not justified, so with only Knowledge/Belief left it must again be counted as mere Belief. The epistemic virtue of truth is therefore lost: an unjustified true belief is lumped together with a false belief. There is no state for true non-knowledge.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous catch-all for ~T&J, T&~J and ~T&~J, and Knowledge is a homogeneous class. The 2x2 distinctions of justification and of truth are no longer tracked in the taxonomy. That is the justification problem and the truth problem that remain once the Gettier case is set aside.

3.text:
With JTB Knowledge = Justified & True & Believed. Let K be the extension of Knowledge and B the extension of Belief as the only other live epistemic category. 
K = J ∧ T ∧ B
¬K = ¬J ∨ ¬T ∨ ¬B

So on a strict Knowledge/Belief dichotomy everything that is not knowledge is forced to be merely Belief. That makes the complement of K far too coarse.

* **Justified false belief.**  J ∧ ¬T ∧ B satisfies justification and belief but fails truth, so by JTB it is not knowledge. On a two state taxonomy it must be classified as plain Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. A justified false belief is creditable in a way an unjustified false belief is not, but JTB has no place to record that credit. The justificatory value of the belief is lost.

* **Unjustified true belief / lucky true belief.** ¬J ∧ T ∧ B satisfies truth and belief but fails justification, so by JTB it is not knowledge. On a two state taxonomy it must again be classified as plain Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and even from a justified false belief J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. A true belief is better off than a false belief, and a lucky true belief is better off than a plain false belief, but JTB has no place to record that truth value. The alethic value of the belief is lost.

Hence the negation of Knowledge in JTB is a disjunction of really different epistemic situations — justified falsehoods and lucky truths — all of which are forced into the single residual category Belief. JTB therefore cannot give a distinct status to a justified false belief and it cannot give a distinct status to an unjustified true belief. The intermediate grades of epistemic merit are collapsed into mere belief.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On a JTB analysis truth and justification are two independent
dimensions. Knowledge is the conjunction

K p = B p & p is true & p is justified for S

so the epistemic space for a subject S with respect to a proposition p is
in fact

 T J   T ~J
J   K p   T ~J B p
~J  J ~T B p   ~T ~J B p

four cells, not two. If the only labels you are allowed to use are
'knowledge' and 'mere belief' you are forced to collapse the 2x2
matrix.

In particular you cannot keep the information carried by justification
separate from the information carried by truth.

* Justified false belief. A belief can be justified for S and still be
false. On JTB such a belief is not knowledge because K requires truth,
but it is not a plain unqualified belief either, it is a justified
belief. With the two-state taxonomy the belief has to be labelled
simply 'belief', and the fact that it is justified is lost. In effect
JTB would have to imply that there is no such thing as a justified
false belief at all, i.e. that justification entails truth, which it
does not.

* Unjustified true belief. A belief can be true and still be
unjustified / lucky for S. On JTB such a belief is not knowledge
because K requires justification, but it is a true belief. Again with
only Knowledge vs Belief there is no place to mark the truth of the
belief without upgrading it to knowledge. You are forced either to call
a true unjustified belief knowledge, which JTB forbids, or to lump a
true justified belief together with a true unjustified belief under the
undifferentiated label 'belief', and lose the justification information.

That is the familiar point that JTB needs at least the four
truth-justification combinations - justified true belief, justified
false belief, unjustified true belief, unjustified false belief - and
hence at least four epistemic categories. Restricting the taxonomy to
Knowledge = justified true belief and Belief = everything else makes
justification and truth inseparable from belief in the way we want
them to be separable. Gettier is set aside, the non-Gettier
collapse is the need for a distinct state for justified false belief
and a distinct state for true but unjustified belief.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The group is converging on the cost of restricting the epistemic taxonomy to Knowledge = Justified True Belief and Belief = everything else, with Gettier set aside.

Common core: JTB treats truth and justification as independent dimensions, giving a 2×2 space T×J: T&J = Knowledge, T&~J = true but unjustified, ~T&J = justified but false, ~T&~J = false and unjustified. With only the labels K and B the 2×2 must be collapsed. The complement of K, ¬K = ¬J ∨ ¬T ∨ ¬B, becomes a heterogeneous waste-basket.

Granularity collapse, in two manifestations:
* Justified false belief, J ∧ ¬T ∧ B, is not knowledge because it fails truth, but with only K/B it has to be classed as mere Belief. It becomes indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The justificatory merit of the belief is lost; justification ceases to be an independent dimension.
* Unjustified true belief / lucky true belief, ¬J ∧ T ∧ B, is not knowledge because it fails justification, but with only K/B it must also be classed as mere Belief. It becomes indistinguishable from a false belief and from a justified false belief. The alethic merit of the belief is lost; truth ceases to be independently trackable for non-knowledge.

Colleagues 2,3,5 explicitly name these as the need for distinct states for justified false belief and for true but unjustified belief, and the consequent loss of information about justification and truth respectively.

The same restriction forces justification to be cashable only in K or B states.
* If a belief p is justified by another belief q, q itself needs justification, requiring r, etc. That yields an infinite regress of justifiers.
* Stopping the chain requires non-inferentially justified basic beliefs, but the menu has no “basic justified” state distinct from K and B. The only stops available are an arbitrary dogmatic foundation, or circular justification. This is the classic Münchhausen trilemma as presented by Colleagues 1,4,6,7.

I am tracking the consensus that the two non-Gettier problems are the collapse of the 2×2 into a waste-basket Belief class — unable to represent justified false belief and unable to represent unjustified true belief separately — and that this collapse is tied to the regress/foundation problem for justification when only K and B are available as reasons. Unresolved nuance: whether the intended “two problems” are the two collapsed cells, or the more general granularity loss plus the regress/stopping problem. Both formulations are being used interchangeably in the thread.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The JTB analysis is K = B ∧ T ∧ J. With only the labels Knowledge and Belief the complement of K is forced to be a single undifferentiated Belief category: ¬K = ¬J ∨ ¬T ∨ ¬B. The epistemic space is in fact Truth × Justification:

T J   T ~J
J   K    true but unjustified
~J  justified false   false and unjustified

Restricting to two states collapses the 2×2 matrix.

The collapse is usually described as two information losses.

* Justified false belief: J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not knowledge because ¬T, so on a K/B dichotomy it must be labelled Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The justificatory virtue of the belief is lost, and justification can no longer be tracked independently of truth. In effect JTB would have to deny the possibility of justified false belief.

* Unjustified true belief / lucky true belief: ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not knowledge because ¬J, so it too must be labelled Belief. It is then indistinguishable from both justified false belief and plain unjustified false belief. The alethic virtue of truth is lost, and truth can no longer be tracked independently of justification. In effect there is no place to mark a true non-knowledge state without upgrading it to knowledge.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous waste-basket for ~T&J, T&~J and ~T&~J, while Knowledge is the homogeneous T&J cell.

Because justification cannot be introduced as a third independent normative status, it has to be cashable in terms of the only available states. A justification for p must be supplied by another epistemic state, either a belief q or a piece of knowledge k. If the justifier is a mere belief it itself needs justification, generating a chain B→B1→B2... With only K and B in the menu there is no non-epistemic basic status to halt the chain. This yields the familiar Münchhausen trilemma for justification on this inventory: infinite regress of justifiers, arbitrary dogmatic foundational stop where some beliefs are treated as justified simply because they are believed, or circular justification. The lack of a distinct justified-non-knowledge state is what forces the regress/foundation dilemma.

No disagreement on the core collapse; colleagues differ only in emphasis between describing the collapse as the two missing cells and describing it as the regress/stopping problem. Gettier is explicitly set aside.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The inventory is restricted to K = Justified True Belief and B = Belief as the only epistemic kinds. On JTB K p = B p & T p & J p. The complement non-K is therefore ¬K = ¬J ∨ ¬T ∨ ¬B, which is forced to be labelled simply ‘Belief’. 

That forces a collapse of the natural Truth × Justification 2×2 matrix

 T J   T ~J
 J   K   T~J B
 ~J  J~T B   ~T~J B

into two labels. The information carried by justification independently of truth, and by truth independently of justification, is lost.

Two distinct information losses are repeatedly flagged:

* Justified false belief J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. By JTB it is not knowledge because ¬T, but on a two-state menu it must be classed as mere Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and from an arbitrary false belief. The justificatory virtue of the belief is lost; justification effectively becomes inseparable from truth, and there is no state for justified non-knowledge.

* Unjustified true belief ¬J ∧ T ∧ B. By JTB it is not knowledge because ¬J, but on a two-state menu it must also be classed as mere Belief. It is then indistinguishable from false beliefs, both justified false and unjustified false. The alethic virtue of truth is lost; a lucky true belief cannot be marked as true without being upgraded to knowledge.

Together Belief becomes a heterogeneous waste-basket for J∧¬T, ¬J∧T and ¬J∧¬T. That is the granularity collapse objection.

Several colleagues re-describe this collapse as a justificatory grounding problem under the two-state restriction. If justification for p must be supplied by another epistemic state, the only candidates are K or B. A justifier that is merely B itself needs justification, giving a chain B p justified by B q justified by B r… This yields the familiar Münchhausen trilemma: infinite regress of justifiers, arbitrary dogmatic foundational stopping point, or circularity. With no distinct justified-but-false or true-but-unjustified state in the menu there is no non-epistemic stopping ground, so justification cannot be cashable in terms of K and B alone without regress or an unexplained basic belief class.

Disagreement in the round: Colleagues 2,3,5 articulate the two problems as the missing justified-false and missing unjustified-true cells. Colleagues 1,4,6,7 articulate them as regress vs arbitrary foundation / loss of granularity. The two descriptions are linked: the missing cells are why justification cannot be tracked independently and why a regress/foundation problem appears when justification is forced to be built only from K and B.

Unresolved: whether the intended “two problems” are framed as the two missing cells versus regress + foundational arbitrariness; the material is the same collapse of the 2×2 space. Gettier is explicitly set aside.

reflection_text.1:
The group is converging on the cost of restricting the epistemic taxonomy to Knowledge = Justified True Belief and Belief = everything else, with Gettier set aside.

Common core: JTB treats truth and justification as independent dimensions, giving a 2×2 space T×J: T&J = Knowledge, T&~J = true but unjustified, ~T&J = justified but false, ~T&~J = false and unjustified. With only the labels K and B the 2×2 must be collapsed. The complement of K, ¬K = ¬J ∨ ¬T ∨ ¬B, becomes a heterogeneous waste-basket.

Granularity collapse, in two manifestations:
* Justified false belief, J ∧ ¬T ∧ B, is not knowledge because it fails truth, but with only K/B it has to be classed as mere Belief. It becomes indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The justificatory merit of the belief is lost; justification ceases to be an independent dimension.
* Unjustified true belief / lucky true belief, ¬J ∧ T ∧ B, is not knowledge because it fails justification, but with only K/B it must also be classed as mere Belief. It becomes indistinguishable from a false belief and from a justified false belief. The alethic merit of the belief is lost; truth ceases to be independently trackable for non-knowledge.

Colleagues 2,3,5 explicitly name these as the need for distinct states for justified false belief and for true but unjustified belief, and the consequent loss of information about justification and truth respectively.

The same restriction forces justification to be cashable only in K or B states.
* If a belief p is justified by another belief q, q itself needs justification, requiring r, etc. That yields an infinite regress of justifiers.
* Stopping the chain requires non-inferentially justified basic beliefs, but the menu has no “basic justified” state distinct from K and B. The only stops available are an arbitrary dogmatic foundation, or circular justification. This is the classic Münchhausen trilemma as presented by Colleagues 1,4,6,7.

I am tracking the consensus that the two non-Gettier problems are the collapse of the 2×2 into a waste-basket Belief class — unable to represent justified false belief and unable to represent unjustified true belief separately — and that this collapse is tied to the regress/foundation problem for justification when only K and B are available as reasons. Both formulations are being used interchangeably in the thread.
reflection_text.2:
The JTB analysis is K = B ∧ T ∧ J. With only the labels Knowledge and Belief the complement of K is forced to be a single undifferentiated Belief category: ¬K = ¬J ∨ ¬T ∨ ¬B. The epistemic space is in fact Truth × Justification:

T J   T ~J
J   K    true but unjustified
~J  justified false   false and unjustified

Restricting to two states collapses the 2×2 matrix.

The collapse is usually described as two information losses.

* Justified false belief: J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not knowledge because ¬T, so on a K/B dichotomy it must be labelled Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The justificatory virtue of the belief is lost, and justification can no longer be tracked independently of truth. In effect JTB would have to deny the possibility of justified false belief.

* Unjustified true belief / lucky true belief: ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not knowledge because ¬J, so it too must be labelled Belief. It is then indistinguishable from both justified false belief and plain unjustified false belief. The alethic virtue of truth is lost, and truth can no longer be tracked independently of justification. In effect there is no place to mark a true non-knowledge state without upgrading it to knowledge.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous waste-basket for ~T&J, T&~J and ~T&~J, while Knowledge is the homogeneous T&J cell.

Because justification cannot be introduced as a third independent normative status, it has to be cashable in terms of the only available states. A justification for p must be supplied by another epistemic state, either a belief q or a piece of knowledge k. If the justifier is a mere belief it itself needs justification, generating a chain B→B1→B2... With only K and B in the menu there is no non-epistemic basic status to halt the chain. This yields the familiar Münchhausen trilemma for justification on this inventory: infinite regress of justifiers, arbitrary dogmatic foundational stop where some beliefs are treated as justified simply because they are believed, or circular justification. The lack of a distinct justified-non-knowledge state is what forces the regress/foundation dilemma.

No disagreement on the core collapse; colleagues differ only in emphasis between describing the collapse as the two missing cells and describing it as the regress/stopping problem. Gettier is explicitly set aside.

1.text:
With JTB

K p := B p & T p & J p

the epistemic space for a fixed subject p is the 2 × 2 Truth × Justification space

T J        T ~J
J   K      T & ~J & B
~J  ~T & J & B   ~T & ~J & B

Knowledge is the one cell T & J & B. On a strict Knowledge / Belief dichotomy

¬K p := ¬J p ∨ ¬T p ∨ ¬B p

is forced to be labelled `mere Belief'. The complement of K is therefore a heterogeneous waste-basket. Two independent pieces of information that JTB treats as
independent are lost in the collapse.

* The justificatory value of a false belief is lost. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not knowledge because it fails truth, but it is a justified belief. With only K/B it has to be labelled B. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B, an unjustified false belief. The taxonomy cannot record the fact that a belief can be justified and still false. In effect the menu is forced to deny the existence of a justified false belief as a distinct normative state, i.e. to make justification entail truth. Justification ceases to be an independent dimension.

* The alethic value of an unjustified true belief is lost. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not knowledge because it fails justification, but it is a true belief. With only K/B it has to be labelled B. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and from J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The taxonomy cannot record the fact that a belief can be true and still unjustified. Truth ceases to be independently trackable for non-knowledge.

Hence Belief = T & ~J & B  ∪  ~T & J & B  ∪  ~T & ~J & B. That is the familiar granularity collapse: JTB needs at least the four truth-justification combinations, and restricting the labels to Knowledge and Belief makes the two non-ideal cells disappear into the same residual category.

This collapse is the source of the justificatory regress problem on the two-state menu. If J p is to be cashable in the inventory, a justifier for p must be a K or a B. A B justifier itself needs justification, so you need q to justify p, r to justify q, etc. With only K and B as the materials for reasons you get the Münchhausen trilemma: an infinite regress of justifiers, an arbitrary dogmatic foundation of beliefs that are taken to be justified simply because they are believed, or circular justification. There is no distinct ‘properly basic justified’ state in which the chain can be stopped non-arbitrarily, so justification cannot be given a non-circular account in terms of Knowledge and Belief alone.

With JTB you really want two independent dimensions: Truth and Justification, with Belief as the attitude that holds across them. That gives the familiar T × J grid:

T & J = Knowledge
T & ~J = true but unjustified
~T & J = justified but false
~T & ~J = false and unjustified

If the only labels you are allowed to use are K = J ∧ T ∧ B and B = ¬K, then everything that is not justified true belief is forced into one residual bucket. The information carried by justification and by truth is no longer tracked separately from belief.

That collapse generates two distinct information losses, and they are the non-Gettier problems of the two-state menu.

1. Loss of justified false belief. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not Knowledge because it fails truth, so on a strict K/B dichotomy it must be called mere Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B, an unjustified false belief. A belief that is properly supported is creditable in a way an arbitrary false belief is not, but the taxonomy has no place to record that credit. Justification ceases to be an independent normative mark.

2. Loss of unjustified true belief. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not Knowledge because it fails justification, so it too must be called mere Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and from J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. A true belief is better off than a false one, and a lucky true belief is in a different position from a plain false belief, but the taxonomy has no place to record that alethic difference without upgrading the belief to Knowledge, which JTB forbids.

In effect Belief becomes a heterogeneous waste-basket for justified falsehoods, lucky truths and completely arbitrary falsehoods. You can no longer say of a belief that it is justified and false, or true and unjustified, without collapsing it into the same state as the opposite case.

The regress / stopping worry that Colleague 1, 4, 6 and 7 raise is real, but on this menu it is a symptom of the same collapse: justification cannot be cashable in terms of K and B alone precisely because K/B no longer lets us mark justified non-knowledge and true non-knowledge as distinct kinds. Once the intermediate cells are erased, the justificatory chain has nowhere non-arbitrary to stop because the states it would need to stop in are not in the inventory.

That is why the literature normally enriches the menu with at least justified false belief and unjustified true belief: without them you cannot keep justification and truth independent of one another in the way JTB itself requires.

* ~T & J & B : justified false belief
* T & ~J & B : unjustified true belief
* ~T & ~J & B : unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge vs Belief we have nowhere to put the first two.

Under the two-state taxonomy it must be labelled ‘mere belief’ and becomes indistinguishable from an unsupported false belief. The justification information is lost.

On JTB it is not knowledge because it fails justification, but it is still a true belief. 2.text:
With JTB K p = B p ∧ T p ∧ J p the natural inventory is Truth × Justification with
belief holding across the four cells

T J : K
T ~J : ¬J ∧ T ∧ B  unjustified true belief
~T J : J ∧ ¬T ∧ B  justified false belief
~T ~J : ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B  unjustified false belief

On a strict Knowledge / Belief menu ¬K p = ¬J p ∨ ¬T p ∨ ¬B p is forced to be
labelled ‘mere Belief’. The complement of Knowledge is then a heterogeneous
waste-basket and justification and truth can no longer be tracked
independently of one another.

* Justified non-knowledge is lost. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not knowledge because ¬T, but
it is a justified belief. With only K/B it must be called Belief and is
epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The justificatory virtue
of a false belief is erased. The taxonomy has no state for justified
non-knowledge, so justification ceases to be an independent normative mark
and is in effect forced to entail truth, J → T.

* True non-knowledge is lost. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not knowledge because ¬J, but it
is a true belief. With only K/B it must again be called Belief and is
epistemically indistinguishable from J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The
alethic virtue of a belief is erased. The taxonomy has no state for true
non-knowledge, so truth ceases to be independently trackable and is in
effect forced to entail justification, T → J.

Hence Belief = T&~J ∪ ~T&J ∪ ~T&~J, while Knowledge = T&J. The two menu-specific
non-Gettier costs are therefore the disappearance of the justified false belief
cell and the disappearance of the unjustified true belief cell. That collapse is
what makes the familiar regress / dogmatic foundation / circularity worry
appear on the two-state inventory: with no distinct J∧¬T and ¬J∧T kinds to
serve as a non-epistemic stop, justification cannot be cashed out in terms of K
and B alone without losing the independence of justification and truth that JTB
is intended to secure.

3.text:
With JTB

K p  :=  B p ∧ T p ∧ J p

the natural space is Truth × Justification with belief holding fixed. That is

         T            ¬T
J   K = J∧T∧B   J∧¬T∧B  justified false belief
¬J  ¬J∧T∧B      ¬J∧¬T∧B  unjustified true belief
                        unjustified false belief

Four cells. On a strict Knowledge / Belief menu

¬K p := ¬J p ∨ ¬T p ∨ ¬B p

is forced to be labelled ‘mere Belief’. The complement of K is then a heterogeneous waste-basket and the two dimensions truth and justification can no longer be tracked independently of one another.

* Justificatory virtue is lost. J∧¬T∧B is not knowledge because ¬T, but it is a justified belief. On K/B it has to be labelled B and is then epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J∧¬T∧B and from ¬J∧T∧B. There is no state for justified non-knowledge. A properly supported false belief is lumped with an unsupported false belief and the fact that it is justified is erased. In effect the menu is forced to deny a distinct justified false belief, i.e. to make J→T.

* Alethic virtue is lost. ¬J∧T∧B is not knowledge because ¬J, but it is a true belief. On K/B it has to be labelled B again and is then indistinguishable from both J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B. There is no state for true non-knowledge. A lucky true belief is lumped with false beliefs and the fact that it is true is erased. In effect the menu is forced to deny a distinct true non-knowledge, i.e. to make T→J.

Hence Belief = T&~J&B ∪ ~T&J&B ∪ ~T&~J&B whereas Knowledge = T&J&B. That is the granularity collapse: with only K and B we cannot say of a belief that it is justified and false, or true and unjustified, without collapsing it into the same residual state as the opposite case.

The same collapse is why justification cannot be cashable in terms of K/B alone. J p must be cashed in other K/B states for q. A B justifier itself needs justification, so with no distinct justified-but-false or true-but-unjustified kind to serve as a non-epistemic stop the chain is the familiar Münchhausen situation: infinite regress, dogmatic foundation or circularity. The regress/foundation worry is the structural expression of the representational loss of the two intermediate cells. Gettier is set aside.

and justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the state-space framing is the clearest way to see what the K/B restriction actually costs us, and it's why I find the collapse argument from C4, C6 and C7 so compelling.

On JTB we want Truth and Justification to be independent dimensions over Belief. That gives us the 2x2:

T & J = Knowledge
T & ~J = unjustified true belief
~T & J = justified false belief
~T & ~J = unjustified false belief

If the only labels we are allowed are K = B & T & J and ¬K = ‘Belief’, then ¬K is forced to be the disjunction ¬J ∨ ¬T ∨ ¬B. Everything that is not justified true belief is poured into one residual bucket.

That is a representational loss, not just a verbal quibble.

First, justified false belief disappears as a distinct normative kind. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not knowledge because it fails truth, but it is creditable in a way an arbitrary false belief is not. On a strict K/B dichotomy it must be called mere Belief and becomes epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The menu can no longer record that a belief can be properly supported and still false. In effect justification is made to entail truth.

Second, unjustified true belief disappears as a distinct alethic kind. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not knowledge because it fails justification, but it is true. On a strict K/B dichotomy it too must be called mere Belief and becomes indistinguishable from both J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The menu can no longer record that a belief can be true and still unjustified. In effect truth is made to entail justification.

Hence Belief = ~T&J ∪ T&~J ∪ ~T&~J is a heterogeneous waste-basket while Knowledge remains the single homogeneous cell T&J. We lose the ability to track justification independently of truth and truth independently of justification, which is exactly what JTB is supposed to let us do.

The Münchhausen trilemma that Colleague 1 raises is real for any reason-giving account of justification, and it can be stopped by foundations even on a K/B inventory. What is specific to limiting the taxonomy to Knowledge and Belief is the information loss just described: there is no place in the menu for a justified non-knowledge and no place for a true non-knowledge. The regress/stopping worry is better understood as a symptom of that collapse, because justification cannot be cashable in K/B terms precisely once the intermediate cells J∧¬T and ¬J∧T are erased from the inventory.

the natural state space is Truth × Justification. Belief is the attitude that is

T & J = Knowledge
T & ~J = unjustified true belief
~T & J = justified false belief
~T & ~J = unjustified false belief

We can no longer record the fact that a belief can be properly supported and still false. In effect justification ceases to be an independent normative mark and is read off as entailing truth.

Second, the alethic value of an unjustified true belief is lost. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not knowledge because it fails justification, but it is a true belief. On the same dichotomy it too must be called Belief and is then indistinguishable from both J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. We can no longer record the fact that a belief can be true and still unjustified. Truth ceases to be independently trackable for non-knowledge.

Hence Belief = ~T&J ∪ T&~J ∪ ~T&~J while Knowledge = T&J. That is the granularity collapse Colleagues 2,3,5 have been describing.

The Münchhausen trilemma about cashing J p in K/B terms – an infinite regress of justifiers, an arbitrary dogmatic foundation, or circularity – is a real worry for any reason-giving account of justification, and Colleague 1 is right that with only K and B as materials for reasons you cannot get a distinct ‘properly basic justified but non-knowledge’ stopping point. That trilemma, however, is not specific to the two-label menu; it is the general problem of giving justification a non-circular account. On the two-state inventory it appears as a symptom of the same collapse: justification cannot be tracked independently of truth precisely because the intermediate cells J∧¬T and ¬J∧T have been erased from the taxonomy.

So the two non-Gettier problems forced by limiting the labels to Knowledge and Belief are the loss of a distinct state for justified false belief and the loss of a distinct state for unjustified true belief. Without them JTB cannot keep justification and truth as the independent dimensions it itself posits.

I think the state-space framing is the clearest way to see what the K/B restriction actually costs us, and it's why I find the collapse argument from C4, C6 and C7 so compelling.

On JTB we want Truth and Justification to be independent dimensions over Belief. That gives us the 2x2:

T & J = Knowledge
T & ~J = unjustified true belief
~T & J = justified false belief
~T & ~J = unjustified false belief

If the only labels we are allowed are K = B & T & J and ¬K = ‘Belief’, then ¬K is forced to be the disjunction ¬J ∨ ¬T ∨ ¬B. Everything that is not justified true belief is poured into one residual bucket.

That is a representational loss, not just a verbal quibble.

First, justified false belief disappears as a distinct normative kind. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not knowledge because it fails truth, but it is creditable in a way an arbitrary false belief is not. On a strict K/B dichotomy it must be called mere Belief and becomes epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The menu can no longer record that a belief can be properly supported and still false. In effect justification is made to entail truth.

Second, unjustified true belief disappears as a distinct alethic kind. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not knowledge because it fails justification, but it is true. On a strict K/B dichotomy it too must be called mere Belief and becomes indistinguishable from both J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. The menu can no longer record that a belief can be true and still unjustified. In effect truth is made to entail justification.

Hence Belief = ~T&J ∪ T&~J ∪ ~T&~J is a heterogeneous waste-basket while Knowledge remains the single homogeneous cell T&J. We lose the ability to track justification independently of truth and truth independently of justification, which is exactly what JTB is supposed to let us do.

The Münchhausen trilemma that Colleague 1 raises is real for any reason-giving account of justification, and it can be stopped by foundations even on a K/B inventory. What is specific to limiting the taxonomy to Knowledge and Belief is the information loss just described: there is no place in the menu for a justified non-knowledge and no place for a true non-knowledge. The regress/stopping worry is better understood as a symptom of that collapse, because justification cannot be cashable in K/B terms precisely once the intermediate cells J∧¬T and ¬J∧T are erased from the inventory.

I'm with Colleagues 2, 4, 6 and 7 on the state-space picture being the clearest way to see what's specific to the K/B restriction.

JTB is K = B & T & J. That commits us to two independent assessment dimensions, Truth and Justification, applied to a belief. The natural inventory is the 2×2:

T & J = Knowledge
T & ~J = unjustified true belief
~T & J = justified false belief
~T & ~J = unjustified false belief

If the only labels we are allowed to use are K and B, then ¬K = ¬J ∨ ¬T ∨ ¬B is forced into a single residual label ‘mere Belief’. Knowledge stays homogeneous while Belief becomes a heterogeneous waste-basket for three epistemically distinct situations.

That forced collapse generates two distinct information losses that are specifically menu-driven, not Gettier problems.

First, the justificatory value of a false belief is lost. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not knowledge because it fails truth, but it is a justified belief. On a strict K/B dichotomy it must be called Belief and is then epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B, an unjustified false belief. We can no longer record the fact that a belief can be properly supported and still false. In effect justification ceases to be an independent normative mark and is read off as entailing truth.

Second, the alethic value of an unjustified true belief is lost. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not knowledge because it fails justification, but it is a true belief. On the same dichotomy it too must be called Belief and is then indistinguishable from both J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. We can no longer record the fact that a belief can be true and still unjustified. Truth ceases to be independently trackable for non-knowledge.

Hence Belief = ~T&J ∪ T&~J ∪ ~T&~J while Knowledge = T&J. That is the granularity collapse Colleagues 2,3,5 have been describing.

The Münchhausen trilemma about cashing J p in K/B terms – an infinite regress of justifiers, an arbitrary dogmatic foundation, or circularity – is a real worry for any reason-giving account of justification, and Colleague 1 is right that with only K and B as materials for reasons you cannot get a distinct ‘properly basic justified but non-knowledge’ stopping point. That trilemma, however, is not specific to the two-label menu; it is the general problem of giving justification a non-circular account. On the two-state inventory it appears as a symptom of the same collapse: justification cannot be tracked independently of truth precisely because the intermediate cells J∧¬T and ¬J∧T have been erased from the taxonomy.

So the two non-Gettier problems forced by limiting the labels to Knowledge and Belief are the loss of a distinct state for justified false belief and the loss of a distinct state for unjustified true belief. Without them JTB cannot keep justification and truth as the independent dimensions it itself posits.

T∧J = Knowledge
T∧~J = unjustified true / lucky true belief
~T∧J = justified false belief
~T∧~J = unjustified false belief
With only K and B labels, ¬K = ¬J ∨ ¬T ∨ ¬B is forced into a single residual ‘mere Belief’. Belief becomes a heterogeneous waste-basket: Belief = T&~J&B ∪ ~T&J&B ∪ ~T&~J&B.

3.text:
With belief held fixed JTB gives the Truth × Justification 2×2

         T               ¬T
J    K = J∧T∧B      J∧¬T∧B  justified false belief
¬J   ¬J∧T∧B         ¬J∧¬T∧B
     unjustified true belief  unjustified false belief

On a strict Knowledge / Belief menu

¬K p := ¬J p ∨ ¬T p ∨ ¬B p

is forced to be labelled ‘mere Belief’. Knowledge remains the single homogeneous cell T∧J∧B while

Belief = T∧¬J∧B  ∪  ¬T∧J∧B  ∪  ¬T∧¬J∧B

is a heterogeneous waste-basket. Justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently.

First, justificatory virtue is lost: no state for justified non-knowledge.
J∧¬T∧B is not knowledge because ¬T, but it is a justified belief. On K/B it must be called Belief and is epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J∧¬T∧B and from ¬J∧T∧B. A properly supported false belief is lumped with an unsupported false belief. The taxonomy can no longer record that a belief can be properly supported and still false. In effect the menu forces J→T, justification ceases to be an independent normative mark; the justified false belief cell disappears.

Second, alethic virtue is lost: no state for true non-knowledge.
¬J∧T∧B is not knowledge because ¬J, but it is a true belief. On K/B it must again be called Belief and is indistinguishable from J∧¬T∧B and from ¬J∧¬T∧B. A lucky true belief is lumped with false beliefs. The taxonomy can no longer record that a belief can be true and still unjustified. In effect the menu forces T→J, truth ceases to be independently trackable for non-knowledge; the unjustified true belief cell disappears.

Hence Belief = ~T&J ∪ T&~J ∪ ~T&~J while Knowledge = T&J. The 2×2 collapses into two labels, which is why justification cannot be cashed out in K/B terms without erasing the independence of J and T that JTB is meant to secure. The familiar regress/foundation pressure is the structural expression of that representational collapse. Gettier is set aside.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m finding the 2x2 Truth × Justification picture very clarifying, and I think C4, C6 and C7 are right to separate what is generic to any reason-giving account of justification from what is specifically forced by a strict K/B menu.

JTB itself commits us to K = B ∧ T ∧ J with T and J meant to be independent dimensions over belief. That naturally gives four cells:

T & J = Knowledge
T & ~J = unjustified true belief
~T & J = justified false belief
~T & ~J = unjustified false belief

On a strict Knowledge / Belief inventory ¬K is forced to be labelled ‘mere Belief’, so ¬K = ¬J ∨ ¬T ∨ ¬B becomes a heterogeneous waste-basket

Belief = T & ~J & B ∪ ~T & J & B ∪ ~T & ~J & B

while Knowledge stays the single homogeneous cell T & J. That is an information loss that is menu-specific, not a Gettier problem.

First, justificatory value is erased. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is not knowledge because ¬T, but it is a justified belief – a properly supported false belief is creditable in a way an arbitrary false belief is not. With only K/B it must be called Belief and becomes epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. There is no distinct state for justified non-knowledge, so the taxonomy forces justification to stop being independently trackable and is in effect read as J → T.

Second, alethic value is erased. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is not knowledge because ¬J, but it is a true belief – a lucky true belief is better off than a false belief. With only K/B it must again be called Belief and becomes indistinguishable from J ∧ ¬T ∧ B and from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B. There is no distinct state for true non-knowledge, so truth ceases to be independently trackable for non-knowledge and is in effect read as T → J.

Those two erasures are the menu-specific non-Gettier costs: no place left in the inventory for a justified false belief and no place left for an unjustified true belief. The Münchhausen pressure about cashing J p in K/B terms, infinite regress vs dogmatic foundation vs circularity, is real for any reason-giving account and it shows up here as a symptom of the collapse, because once the J∧¬T and ¬J∧T cells are erased justification can no longer be given an independent stopping point in K/B terms. The distinct problems asked for by the two-label restriction are the representational losses above, not the generic justification regress per se.

The JTB analysis is K p = B p ∧ T p ∧ J p. With Belief held fixed the natural space is Truth × Justification: T∧J = Knowledge; T∧¬J = unjustified true / lucky true belief; ¬T∧J = justified false belief; ¬T∧¬J = unjustified false belief. Restricting the taxonomy to K/B forces ¬K p := ¬J p ∨ ¬T p ∨ ¬B p to be labelled ‘mere Belief’. The complement of Knowledge is therefore the heterogeneous waste-basket Belief = T∧¬J∧B ∪ ¬T∧J∧B ∪ ¬T∧¬J∧B, so justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently.

Menu-specific information losses, now the consensus focal point in rounds 0-3:

* Justificatory value lost. J∧¬T∧B is not knowledge by lack of truth but is a justified belief. On K/B it must be called B and is epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J∧¬T∧B. There is no distinct state for justified non-knowledge; a properly supported false belief is lumped with an unsupported false belief, in effect forcing J→T.
* Alethic value lost. ¬J∧T∧B is not knowledge by lack of justification but is a true belief. On K/B it must be called B and is indistinguishable from J∧¬T∧B and ¬J∧¬T∧B. There is no distinct state for true non-knowledge; a lucky true belief is lumped with false beliefs, in effect forcing T→J.

Hence Belief = ~T&J ∪ T&~J ∪ ~T&~J while Knowledge = T&J. This is the granularity collapse: loss of a cell for justified false belief and loss of a cell for unjustified true belief.

Justification regress/foundation pressure. With only K and B as materials for reasons, J p must be cashed in K/B terms. A justifier is itself K or B, and a B justifier needs its own justifier, producing Münchhausen trilemma pressure: infinite regress, arbitrary dogmatic foundation, or circularity. No non-epistemic stopping point is available in the two-state menu.

3.text:
With belief held fixed JTB is Truth × Justification

T & J    = K = B∧T∧J
T & ¬J   = unjustified true belief
¬T & J   = justified false belief
¬T & ¬J  = unjustified false belief

On a strict Knowledge / Belief menu ¬K p := ¬J p ∨ ¬T p ∨ ¬B p is forced to be called ‘mere Belief’. Knowledge stays the single homogeneous cell T∧J∧B while

Belief = T∧¬J∧B ∪ ¬T∧J∧B ∪ ¬T∧¬J∧B

is a heterogeneous waste-basket. Justification and truth can no longer be tracked independently for non-knowledge.

That forced granularity collapse is two menu-specific information losses.

* Justificatory virtue lost, no distinct state for justified non-knowledge.
J∧¬T∧B is not knowledge because ¬T, but it is a justified belief. On K/B it must be labelled Belief and is epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J∧¬T∧B and from ¬J∧T∧B. A properly supported false belief is lumped with an unsupported false belief. The taxonomy can no longer record that a belief can be properly supported and still false; in effect the menu forces J→T for non-knowledge and justification ceases to be an independent normative mark. The justified false belief cell disappears.

* Alethic virtue lost, no distinct state for true non-knowledge.
¬J∧T∧B is not knowledge because ¬J, but it is a true belief, the lucky true belief. On K/B it must again be labelled Belief and is indistinguishable from J∧¬T∧B and from ¬J∧¬T∧B. A lucky true belief is lumped with false beliefs. The taxonomy can no longer record that a belief can be true and still unjustified; in effect the menu forces T→J for non-knowledge and truth ceases to be independently trackable for non-knowledge. The unjustified true belief cell disappears.

Hence Belief = ~T&J ∪ T&~J ∪ ~T&~J while Knowledge = T&J. We lose a place for a justified false belief and a place for an unjustified true belief, i.e. the ability to keep justification and truth as independent dimensions of assessment for non-knowledge, which is exactly what JTB posits.

The Münchhausen regress / dogmatic foundation / circularity pressure that appears when J p must be cashed in K/B terms is the structural expression of that representational collapse, not a distinct menu-specific problem over and above the loss of the J∧¬T and ¬J∧T cells. Gettier is set aside.
